03 / Causal experiment

Hold the world constant. Change the information.

Run a baseline and a treatment with the same seed, valuations, agents, and fundamental. Expose selected agents to a message and measure the difference.

Same market conditionsOne controlled intervention
Baseline vs. information treatment
ILLUSTRATIVE PATHS
BaselineTreatment
The intervention changes information, not the underlying fundamental. Lines illustrate the method; they are not empirical Q1 results.
04 / Economic mechanism

A trade creates measurable surplus.

With buyer value $112 and seller cost $88, a transaction at $102 generates $10 buyer surplus and $14 seller surplus. Total gains from trade: $24.

Buyer surplus = value − priceSeller surplus = price − cost
Surplus decomposition / illustrative trade

Transaction price $102

Example arithmetic, not measured Q1 results. Allocative efficiency compares realized surplus with the feasible maximum.

06 / Measurement

Not just what agents say. What their actions change.

Quantify bid shifts, reaction latency, price displacement, recovery, information propagation, and allocative efficiency.

CoAgentics / Research objective

Make autonomous economic behavior observable, testable, and reproducible.

Use market mechanisms as an experimental instrument to study multi-agent decision-making—and build evidence for understanding and evaluating increasingly autonomous systems.

From incentives → actions → outcomes → evidence.
